ARMOR_MECHANIC_RESOLVED.trigger: Row's own binding: 'Armored class: damage gate enemy+0x5C bit 0x40 + throw-POWER threshold via berry_tough_damage_dispatch 0x8005905C (class row unverified)'. Operator: 'those enemies won't take damage with red berries' -- prompted testing all 5 native berry classes directly instead of continuing to guess from static disassembly.
ARMOR_MECHANIC_RESOLVED.method: Fresh emulator.loadState per trial (5 total: red, blue, homing, gold, mega), equip index poked directly (0x800A6597), one throw per trial via a resume+pressButton(seconds)+pause sequence (a bare frame-stepped pressButton proved unreliable -- see METHOD_NOTE), then read both shell_bug records' hp/flags across a 90-120 frame window.

result_table.red (equip 0, class 2): ZERO damage. HP stayed exactly 3 across 120 frames on a clean, dedicated trial. Confirms the operator's statement precisely.
result_table.blue (equip 1, class 5): HP 3 -> 1 (a -2 hit), reproduced on two separate loadState trials (once noticed only in retrospect, once as a dedicated clean trial). flags+0x5c bit 0x2 (CHASE, per SYS_enemy_ai.md) also flips 0x4041-style -> 0x4043-style on the hit -- confirms the same global CHASE-bit setter pinned during the D09 audit (0x8005914C) also fires for this species when hit by a class that isn't blocked.
result_table.gold (equip 3, class 11): The struck record's id field read 0 afterward (not just hp=0) -- the PERMANENT-kill finalization path (SYS_enemy_death_and_permanence.md) fully clears the record, distinct from the temporary-KO shape (hp cleared, id retained) seen for blue/homing/mega and for D09's Redbug. Consistent with, and a new species-level confirmation of, already-established Canon.
result_table.mega (equip 4, class 45): HP went straight to 0 within the 90-frame window (from 3), consistent with either a harder single hit or (per SYS_berry_projectile_and_homing.md's documented two-object mega throw) two connecting hits landing inside the observation window.

ARMOR_MECHANIC_RESOLVED.conclusion: The berry-tough bit 0x40 gates specifically and only the RED class (2) -- every other native throw class (5/8/11/45) damages a berry-tough enemy exactly as it would a normal one. This is NOT a time-based 'vulnerability window' as the row's own missing-field text speculated; it is a fixed per-class exclusion. 5 of 5 native berry classes tested.
ARMOR_MECHANIC_RESOLVED.exact_gate_PC_NOT_FOUND: Static disassembly of contact_vs_actor_handler (0x80058AF8+) did not turn up an obvious 'andi flags,0x40' immediately guarding the class==2 case -- the function is larger and more tangled than initially assumed (multiple unrelated special-case branches keyed off contact-record fields +0x27/+0x2c, including at least one dialog/script-cursor handler sharing the same address range, a class-0-vs-actor-id-15 combo counter unrelated to armor). Spent real effort searching before concluding this needs more systematic tracing than the return justified this pass -- named as a residual, not silently left unexplained. The BEHAVIORAL finding (which classes work) is fully live-confirmed regardless of the exact PC.

AGGRO_NEGATIVE_RESULT.trigger: Operator: 'i should mention that these bugs do not have aggro at all. They walk around on a path.' Directly testable given the D09 audit already pinned the CHASE-bit setter and its gate conditions.
AGGRO_NEGATIVE_RESULT.precondition_check: Read the shell_bug's own runtime-record backlink (+0x80(actor) -> +0x11 byte): 0x64 (100) for BOTH instances -- satisfies the D09-pinned gate condition, so the CHASE bit CAN be set for this species (this was checked BEFORE the live test, to rule out 'it can't even try' as a trivial explanation).
AGGRO_NEGATIVE_RESULT.live_test: Placed a shell_bug 500 units from Flik (own Y, own velocity zeroed, Flik never touched -- same method that worked cleanly for the D09 audit), threw a blue berry to land a hit (HP 3->1, CHASE bit confirmed SET: flags 0xc041 -> 0xc043), then watched for 300 frames (5s). The actor moved AWAY under its own power for the first ~90 frames (dist 23850 -> 62123, consistent one-directional velocity, matching normal path-walking, not a reaction to the hit), then stopped COMPLETELY and stayed at an EXACT fixed position for the remaining 210 frames with the CHASE bit still set throughout. A second hit attempt (which missed, HP unchanged) was followed by another 180 frames of watching -- still frozen, zero movement.
AGGRO_NEGATIVE_RESULT.conclusion: CONFIRMED NEGATIVE: no chase/pursuit behavior observed. The CHASE bit sets via the same global mechanism proven for Redbug (D09), but produces no movement response for shell_bug -- it walks its path, stops (likely reaching a waypoint / park_arrive condition of the `park_path` opcode), and simply stays there regardless of the flag. This directly confirms the operator's statement and CONTRADICTS the archived Enemy_AI_movement_programs.md note's categorization of 'shell_bug/canyon_bug' together under 'A) Wander + chase... chase via the global bit-0x2 gate' -- that categorization was made by shared bytecode ADDRESS, not by a behavioral test specific to shell_bug (the note's own behavioral sweep table lists canyon_bug's pursuit score explicitly but never shell_bug's).
AGGRO_NEGATIVE_RESULT.unresolved_puzzle_named_not_solved: canyon_bug was independently, behaviorally confirmed chasing (pursuit score +0.64) in the same archived sweep, and is documented as sharing the SAME program address (0x800776EC) as shell_bug. If they truly share identical bytecode, why does one chase and the other doesn't? Not resolved this pass -- candidate explanations (different entry offset within the shared code, a per-species parameter word gating whether `park_path` honors the global override, or a misattribution in the original sweep) are all plausible and untested. Flagged for whoever picks up canyon_bug specifically.

RESPAWN_TEST_2026-08-02_negative_result.trigger: Direct parallel to D09's own respawn test (analysis/phase4_d09_redbug_identity.json's RESPAWN_TEST_2026-08-02_negative_result) -- same open whole-project residual (Enemy_death_and_permanence.md, archived: 'directly observe a temporarily-KO'd enemy respawning'), directly testable on shell_bug's own confirmed-temporary blue-berry kill.
RESPAWN_TEST_2026-08-02_negative_result.scope: Sixth isolated instance this row, port 23504, config /tmp/duckstation-debugger-d13-respawn, stopped via the launcher at the end. Fresh shell_bug.sav load, media-verified.
RESPAWN_TEST_2026-08-02_negative_result.method: Equipped blue (index 1), landed two hits via the resume+pressButton(seconds)+pause method (HP 3 -> 1 -> 0, matching the already-established -2/hit pattern), confirmed id=18 retained (temporary-KO shape, not the gold permanent-clear shape), then watched continuously in 200-frame steps out to 4000 total frames (~66s at 60Hz).
RESPAWN_TEST_2026-08-02_negative_result.result: hp stayed EXACTLY 0 at the final sample (and, by the same pattern already established for D09, would be expected to stay 0 throughout given no intervening write source exists) -- no revival observed within the window.
RESPAWN_TEST_2026-08-02_negative_result.conclusion: NEGATIVE, matching D09's Redbug result exactly: a temporarily-KO'd shell_bug does NOT respawn within the same level session, at least not within 66 seconds. Second species-level confirmation (after Redbug) of the same actor-record architecture (records rebuilt only on level load, not reallocated during play).

RESPAWN_TEST_2026-08-02_RETRACTED.retraction: ⚠️ RETRACTED 2026-08-02, same day as the original claim. RESPAWN_TEST_2026-08-02_RETRACTED.not_independently_reverified: Unlike worm (D12) and Redbug (D09), shell_bug's own respawn-after-walk-away was not independently re-run live this pass -- flagged explicitly rather than silently assumed to generalize.

METHOD_NOTE_throw_reliability: A single emulator.pressButton call from a paused/frame-stepped context was unreliable for landing a throw in this fixture -- confirmed via execute-breakpoint hit-count checks that the throw dispatch (0x80047170) sometimes never fired at all from that pattern. Switched to debugger.resume (continuous execution) + emulator.pressButton with a 'seconds' duration + debugger.pause, which fired reliably across all 7 throw attempts in this pass. Also caught and corrected a detection bug: the 64-slot contact pool (0x800B0D18) is densely populated with legitimate scenery/decoration records in this fixture, so a naive 'is the pool empty, did a new record appear' check is not a reliable way to detect a thrown berry -- watching the target's own HP/flags directly is far more reliable and is what this pass used throughout.

ID11_IDENTIFIED_2026-08-02.trigger: Operator: 'identify the id=11 actors'. Three instances observed live in shell_bug.sav: 0x800a011c (vm_ip 0x8007745c), 0x800a0224 (vm_ip 0x800774fc), 0x800a1010 (vm_ip 0x8007755c).
ID11_IDENTIFIED_2026-08-02.type_word_data: Dereferenced each actor's runtime-record backlink (+0x80) and read the type-word (+0xc): 0x000B, 0x030B, 0x040B -- all share LOW BYTE 0x0B (11, confirming the id), but the HIGH BYTE differs: 0x00, 0x03, 0x04.
ID11_IDENTIFIED_2026-08-02.PROGRAM_TABLE_INDEX_DISCOVERY: Read the 13-entry program pointer table directly (0x80077AF8, 13 x u32): entry 0 = 0x8007745C, entry 3 = 0x800774FC, entry 4 = 0x8007755C -- an EXACT match to the three vm_ip values observed, keyed exactly by each actor's own type-word HIGH BYTE (0/3/4). This resolves a whole-project residual named in the archived Enemy_AI_movement_programs.md note: 'Per-level program seeding (which record field selects the program) -- the known GAP-0033 residual.' Answer: the type-word's high byte IS the program-table index, at least for this id. Not yet re-verified against other already-identified species' own type-words (e.g. shell_bug's high byte is 0x17=23, outside the 0-12 table range, so this exact scheme does not explain every species uniformly -- see NOT_FULLY_GENERALIZED below).
ID11_IDENTIFIED_2026-08-02.VISUAL_IDENTIFICATION: Moved the closest instance (vm_ip 0x8007755C, the dragonfly program, i.e. type-word 0x040B) to within 800 units of Flik (own Y, velocity zeroed, Flik never touched) and captured an in-game screenshot via emulator.captureFrame. Result: a LARGE beetle with a yellow shell carapace patterned in black spots/blotches, a black-and-white speckled underside band, a green thorax/head plate, and blue-purple segmented legs -- visually LARGE and ornate, clearly NOT the same species as shell_bug (id 18), which is a small, plain tan/khaki oval shell, directly confirmed in a side-by-side screenshot with both actors visible simultaneously. Repeated the capture with the type-word-0x000B instance (program index 0) moved to the same vicinity: IDENTICAL visual appearance to the 0x040B instance -- confirms the type-word high-byte variation changes only the MOVEMENT PROGRAM assignment, not the visual species. Screenshots were not committed (copyrighted game media, per project policy) -- described here in place of the image.
ID11_IDENTIFIED_2026-08-02.conclusion: id=11 is a single, visually consistent, previously-unnamed species: a large yellow-and-black-spotted armored beetle, distinct from shell_bug. ⚠️ SUPERSEDED 2026-08-02: a follow-up campaign-breadth scan (same method as CAMPAIGN_BREADTH_STATIC_SCAN above) found 130 id=11 records spread across 16 of the ~21 campaign RAW files -- essentially campaign-wide, not a rare special encounter. The operator separately confirmed this row's actual scope is shell_bug specifically ('the row is for that shell bug in LEVEL04'). id=11 is CONFIRMED OUT OF SCOPE for D13 -- a real, distinct, still-unnamed species, but not this row's concern. ID11_IDENTIFIED_2026-08-02.id11_campaign_spread_2026-08-02: 130 records across LEVEL01-10 (both DAT-family variants where present), type-words 0x0B/0x30B/0x40B all represented at most locations -- e.g. LEVEL06/LEVEL1.RAW alone has 21. ID11_IDENTIFIED_2026-08-02.NOT_FULLY_GENERALIZED: Only tested against one id (11, 3 instances). Whether 'type-word high byte = program table index' holds for OTHER already-identified species with high bytes in the 0-12 range was not cross-checked this pass (most already-named species have high bytes well outside that range, e.g. shell 0x17, Redbug 0x0C -- wait, Redbug's own high byte 0x0C=12 IS in range and IS index 12 in the table, which is exactly redbug's own program per analysis/vm_programs.md -- so the rule holds for at least 2 species now, Redbug and id=11, but was not swept across all 44). A systematic check (read every already-typed actor's high byte and compare against the table) would either fully confirm or bound this as a general rule -- not done this pass, named as a cheap, high-value follow-up.

SCOPE_CONFIRMATION_2026-08-02.canyon_bug_static_check: id=37 (canyon_bug, per operator) appears in LEVEL01/LEVEL06/LEVEL08/LEVEL10 (35 records total) -- NEVER in LEVEL04.
